name: Record crew time and cost codes
summary: Every week each self-perform crew's foreman records the hours of every worker by day and cost code, the general foreman approves the sheet, and payroll keys it into the ERP so the crew is paid on Thursday and the labour cost lands on the right budget line. In 2019-2022 most crews still used paper crew sheets, some used tablet apps. The process is slow because sheets wait for the end of the week, for the general foreman's drive between sites and for the Monday payroll cut-off, and error-prone because cost codes are written by hand under time pressure. Miscoded hours distort the cost forecast and are usually found a week or two later by project controls.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 1,330 unionised hourly carpenters, finishers and labourers in roughly 135 crews on about 220 projects.
baseline.notes: One case is one crew's weekly sheet, from Monday's first entry to the hours being accepted in job cost.

trigger: A self-perform crew starts its work week on a project.
end_state: The crew's hours are paid through the weekly payroll and accepted, or reclassified, by project controls in job cost.

volume.seasonality: Fewer crews from December to March and more from May to October, following the field workforce of about 1,050 in winter and 1,700 in summer.

evidence.note: About 1,330 hourly workers in crews of 8 to 12 gives about 135 crews x 4.33 weeks = 580 sheets a month; matches the organisation file.
Summer field workforce of about 1,700 against an average of 1,330 in the organisation file.
About 2 hours a week per crew sheet x 580 sheets a month / 130 productive hours.
About 45 minutes per sheet including travel, 580 sheets a month.
About 40 minutes per sheet logging, keying, fixing and balancing.

roles.title: Project controls specialist (cost)
roles.department: Operations support (project controls, scheduling, VDC, quality)

evidence.note: Weekly labour review and reclasses; small share of 25 specialists' time.
Posting reclasses only.

systems.name: Field time capture (paper sheets or tablet app keyed to cost codes)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Open the crew sheet for the week
steps.description: On Monday morning the foreman takes a blank weekly crew sheet (or opens the tablet form) pre-printed with the crew names, union local, classification and the project's cost code list issued by project controls. He crosses off workers who left and writes in anyone added by the general foreman.

error.defect_description: Crew list out of date: a new hire is missing or a laid-off worker still listed.

evidence.note: Daily foreman timesheet by job and employee is standard construction ERP practice.

steps.name: Record daily hours by cost code
steps.description: At the end of each shift Monday to Thursday the foreman writes each worker's hours against the cost codes the crew worked on (forms, rebar placing, pour, strip), splits overtime from straight time and notes travel or board allowance days. He often fills two or three days at once from memory when the site is busy.

error.defect_description: Hours on the wrong cost code, a transposed code, or a worker's hours missed or rounded.

evidence.note: Foremen select cost codes daily; share of miscoded sheets is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Finish the week and add premiums
steps.description: On Friday (or Saturday when the crew works a sixth day) the foreman records the last day, totals each worker's straight time, overtime and double time, and marks shift premiums, travel time and board allowance entitlements under the collective agreement.

error.defect_description: Overtime or premium hours put in the straight-time column, or allowance days missed.

next.condition: crew sent home for rain or cold on one day

evidence.note: Agreements set a four- or five-day week of 8 to 10 hours with premiums (art. 20, 24); the wait is the working week itself.

steps.name: Record a weather day and reporting time
steps.description: When rain, wind or cold stops concrete or crane work, the foreman waits to see whether the weather clears, then sends the crew home and records the reporting-time pay the agreement guarantees and the hours actually worked. He notes the lost day in the daily report so the superintendent can track weather delay.

error.defect_description: Reporting time missed or claimed for workers who did not show up.

evidence.note: Reporting-time pay articles are common in ICI agreements (art. 23 in the BACU agreement has the heading); weather days roughly one week in seven over a year is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Crew members check and initial their hours
steps.description: Before leaving on the last day the foreman reads out or shows each worker his hours and allowances, and each worker initials the paper sheet or taps acknowledge on the tablet. Disagreements are fixed on the spot.

control.basis: Collective agreement: timesheets for members are mandatory and signed copies go with the pay (BACU-Guild ICI art. 22.01)

evidence.note: Art. 22.01: timesheets mandatory, paper or electronic. Paper share of 65% in 2019-2022 is the author's estimate.

steps.name: General foreman drives to collect paper sheets
steps.description: The general foreman, who looks after several crews on two or three sites, drives between sites on Friday afternoon or Monday morning to pick up the paper sheets left in the site trailer.

error.defect_description: A sheet left in the trailer or lost in the truck.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: travel time per crew sheet when one general foreman covers three to five crews.

steps.name: General foreman reviews and approves crew hours
steps.description: The general foreman compares each sheet with the crew plan and the daily reports: crew size, days worked, overtime authorised and whether the cost codes match the work done (no forming hours on a code that was finished last week). He signs the sheet or approves it on the tablet.

error.defect_description: Approves a sheet without catching a miscoded day.

control.basis: Company timekeeping policy: supervisor approval of hours and overtime before payroll

evidence.note: Approval by the general foreman follows the organisation's process description; return rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Foreman corrects the sheet
steps.description: The general foreman phones or meets the foreman; the foreman checks his notes, moves hours to the right cost code, adds missed overtime or removes a worker who was absent, and resubmits the sheet.

error.defect_description: Correction introduces a new keying error.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send approved sheets to payroll by the Monday cut-off
steps.description: The general foreman scans or photographs paper sheets and emails them to the regional payroll inbox, or submits the tablet batch, before the end of Monday so that payday is not held up.

control.basis: Collective agreement timesheet deadline: end of business day Monday after the workweek (BACU-Guild ICI art. 22.01)

evidence.note: Art. 22.01 sets the Monday deadline for paper timesheets.

steps.name: Payroll logs the sheet against the expected crew list
steps.description: A payroll specialist ticks the crew off the weekly list of expected sheets for the region and checks that every page is legible and signed. Missing or unreadable sheets are chased before the Tuesday batch closes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the share of crews whose sheets are late or unreadable in a given week.

steps.name: Payroll chases the missing or unreadable sheet
steps.description: The payroll specialist emails and then phones the general foreman or foreman, explaining that the crew will not be paid on Thursday without the sheet, and asks for a resend or for the hours by phone with the signed copy to follow.

evidence.note: Art. 22.01 lets a timesheet be submitted by telephone, email or fax with the signed copy to follow; effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Key hours into the payroll timecard batch
steps.description: For paper sheets the payroll specialist types each worker's daily hours into the ERP timecard batch by job, cost code, earning type (straight time, overtime, double time), union local and classification; tablet batches are imported and spot-checked. A crew of ten over five days is fifty or more lines.

error.defect_description: Keying error: transposed cost code, hours on the wrong day or wrong earning type.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 30 seconds per line for 50 lines; less for imported tablet batches.

steps.name: ERP edits check the timecard lines
steps.description: The ERP checks each line when the batch is validated: employee active and set up for that union local, job and cost code open, classification rate on file, and daily hours under a limit. Lines that fail are listed on an edit report.

evidence.note: Standard construction ERP payroll edit report; share with errors is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve timecard edit errors
steps.description: The payroll specialist works the edit report: a closed cost code, a new hire not yet set up, a worker keyed under the wrong local. She fixes keying errors herself, asks HR for a missing set-up, and sends cost code questions to project controls.

error.defect_description: Fix moves hours to a plausible but wrong code.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Project controls assigns or opens the cost code
steps.description: The project controls specialist decides which budget line the hours belong to, for example a new code for change-order work that must be tracked for pricing, opens it in the ERP and replies to payroll.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check batch totals against the sheet
steps.description: The payroll specialist compares the hours and head count in the ERP batch with the totals written on the sheet and ticks the sheet as entered.

control.basis: Internal control over payroll: batch totals agreed to source documents before the run

evidence.note: Common payroll batch control; author's estimate of time.

steps.name: Timecard batch closes for the payroll run
steps.description: The ERP locks the region's timecard batch at the Tuesday cut-off; no more lines can be added, and the batch is handed to the weekly payroll calculation for the Thursday payday.

evidence.note: Time books close weekly and pay follows by Thursday (art. 22.02).

steps.name: Labour hours and cost post to job cost
steps.description: When the payroll run is posted (after the Thursday payday) the ERP writes each worker's hours and burdened labour cost to the job and cost code, where they appear on the weekly labour report.

evidence.note: Thursday payday within four working days of closing the books (art. 22.02); posting timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Project controls reviews weekly labour by cost code
steps.description: The project controls specialist runs the weekly labour report and compares hours and unit costs by cost code with the budget and the quantities in the daily reports, looking for hours on finished codes, codes with hours but no progress, and crews charged to the wrong project.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: share of crew-weeks with a miscoding large enough to correct.

steps.name: Draft the labour cost reclass
steps.description: The project controls specialist lists the hours and dollars to move between cost codes or jobs, with the reason, and sends the reclass request to the project accountant.

error.defect_description: Reclass amount does not match the hours moved.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Project accountant posts the reclass
steps.description: The project accountant checks the reclass request against the job cost detail and posts a job cost adjustment in the ERP so that the next cost report and forecast use the corrected figures.

control.basis: Journal and job cost adjustments posted by accounting, not by the requester

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Hours questioned by the general foreman
exceptions.description: Wrong cost code, missed overtime or an absent worker on the sheet; the foreman corrects and resubmits.

exceptions.name: Late or unreadable sheet
exceptions.description: Payroll chases the general foreman before the Tuesday batch closes; if it is still missing the crew risks being paid late.

exceptions.name: Weather day
exceptions.description: The crew is sent home and reporting-time pay is recorded.

exceptions.name: Miscoded hours found in job cost
exceptions.description: Project controls finds hours on the wrong code a week or more later and has them reclassified.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the first day of the work week to hours accepted in job cost
benchmarks.population: Union ICI crews paid weekly, Ontario

evidence.note: Derived: a five-day week, sheets due Monday (art. 22.01), payday Thursday within four working days of closing the books (art. 22.02), then about a day for posting and review.

pain_points.description: Cost codes written by hand at the end of the day are often wrong or transposed, so the weekly labour report and the cost forecast are wrong until project controls finds and reclassifies them.

evidence.note: Vendor material on daily crew time by cost code; frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Paper sheets wait for the general foreman's drive between sites, and a sheet that misses the Monday cut-off puts the Thursday payday at risk, with a two-hour-a-day late pay penalty in some agreements.
Payroll re-keys every paper sheet line by line into the ERP.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the paper share in 2019-2022.

sources.title: BACU-Guild Province Wide ICI Collective Agreement (marble, tile, terrazzo, cement masons, resilient floor layers and helpers), 1 April 2022 to 30 April 2025
sources.publisher: Brick and Allied Craft Union of Canada and Terrazzo, Tile & Marble Guild of Ontario; filed with Employment and Social Development Canada (Negotech)

sources.title: Timesheets
sources.supports: Field teams enter time for individuals or crews on mobile or web; foremen select cost codes daily; approval processes; export to payroll or ERP.

sources.title: PR Daily Foreman Timesheet
sources.supports: Construction ERP payroll report printed as a daily foreman timesheet, sorted by job and employee, designed to be filled out and entered daily.

assumptions: The case runs from Monday's first entry to job cost acceptance, so the working week itself (about 4 to 5 days) is in the wait before s03.
Paper sheets 65%, tablet entry 35% in 2019-2022; tablet sheets skip the general foreman's collection drive.
Recording daily hours (s02) happens during the shift days and overlaps the opening of the sheet; it is listed in sequence with no wait.
Posting to job cost (s18) depends on the weekly payroll run documented in gc-fin-union-payroll.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (about 1.6 loading on union wages, 1.35 on salaries).
The organisation file lists foreman, general-foreman and payroll-specialist for this process; project-controls and project-accountant are added because they review and correct the cost coding.
